title.es: Señalizar el recorrido de una charla

es: Reconocer y ordenar las expresiones que señalizan la apertura, las transiciones, los desvíos y el cierre de una charla, y elegir la fórmula adecuada para cada momento.

teaching.en: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming: today I will present the results of our neighbourhood survey, which reached more than six hundred households.
teaching.es: Buenos días a todos y gracias por venir: hoy presentaré los resultados de nuestra encuesta del barrio, que llegó a más de seiscientos hogares.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura: saludo + agradecimiento + I will present… anuncia el tema y un dato sitúa al público.
segments: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming: today I will present the
results of our neighbourhood survey, which reached more than six hundred households.
teaching.audioText: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming: today I will present the results of our neighbourhood survey, which reached more than six hundred households.

teaching.en: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain how we collected the data, before I turn to what residents told us.
teaching.es: Expondré la charla en tres partes y, en primer lugar, explicaré cómo recogimos los datos, antes de pasar a lo que nos dijeron los vecinos.
teaching.explanationEs: I will outline… anuncia el esquema; firstly abre la primera parte y before… deja ver la siguiente.
segments: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain
how we collected the data, before I turn to what residents told us.
teaching.audioText: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain how we collected the data, before I turn to what residents told us.

teaching.en: Now that the method is clear, let's move on to the results, and I will touch on the most surprising figures only briefly.
teaching.es: Ahora que el método está claro, pasemos a los resultados, y mencionaré solo de pasada las cifras más sorprendentes.
teaching.explanationEs: Let's move on to + parte es la transición habitual; touch on = tratar algo por encima, sin detenerse.
segments: Now that the method is clear, let's move on to the results,
and I will touch on the most surprising figures only briefly.
teaching.audioText: Now that the method is clear, let's move on to the results, and I will touch on the most surprising figures only briefly.

teaching.en: Good speakers signpost every stage of a talk, and if they digress, they say so openly and return to the main point.
teaching.es: Los buenos oradores señalizan cada etapa de una charla y, si se desvían del tema, lo dicen abiertamente y vuelven al punto principal.
teaching.explanationEs: Signpost es el verbo de marcar el camino al público; digress = apartarse del tema, y se avisa.
segments: Good speakers signpost every stage of a talk, and if they
digress, they say so openly and return to the main point.
teaching.audioText: Good speakers signpost every stage of a talk, and if they digress, they say so openly and return to the main point.

teaching.en: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise, which worried more residents than any other issue in our survey.
teaching.es: Ahora me gustaría pasar al tema del ruido, que preocupó a más vecinos que cualquier otro asunto de nuestra encuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Now I'd like to turn to + tema: transición algo más formal; el tema va con the question of…
segments: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise, which
worried more residents than any other issue in our survey.
teaching.audioText: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise, which worried more residents than any other issue in our survey.

teaching.en: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights; finally, I will be glad to take any questions you may have.
teaching.es: En resumen, la mayoría de los vecinos quiere calles más seguras y noches más tranquilas; por último, responderé con gusto a las preguntas que tengan.
teaching.explanationEs: Cierre: To sum up + idea principal; finally anuncia el último paso y take questions abre el turno de preguntas.
segments: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights; finally,
I will be glad to take any questions you may have.
teaching.audioText: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights; finally, I will be glad to take any questions you may have.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple este fragmento dentro de una charla?

choices.text: It moves the audience on from the method to the results.
It sums up the conclusions before the final questions.
It opens the talk and announces how it will be organised.

feedback.es: El saludo, «I will outline» y «firstly» forman una apertura: anuncian el esquema. Una transición usaría move on to y un cierre, to sum up.

hint.es: Fíjate en cómo empieza el texto y en lo que anuncia que hará el orador.

origin.text: Good morning, everyone. Over the next ten minutes I will outline three findings from our neighbourhood survey, and firstly I want to explain why we asked these questions at all.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ahora me gustaría pasar al tema del ruido.»

feedback.es: Turn to + tema es la transición formal para cambiar de parte; el verbo turn va seguido de to.

hint.es: Es el verbo que también significa «girar».

origin.text: We have covered the method, so the audience is ready for the next part. Now I'd like to ___ to the question of noise, which worries residents more than anything else.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por último, responderé con gusto a sus preguntas.»

answer.text: Finally I will be happy to take your questions

feedback.es: Finally anuncia el último paso de la charla y take questions es la fórmula que abre el turno de preguntas.

hint.es: Empieza con Finally y termina con las preguntas.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué hizo la oradora a mitad de la charla.

choices.text: She told a story about her street, having warned the audience first.
She jumped ahead to what the council should do.
She lost her place and needed the audience to steer her back.

feedback.es: A mitad de la charla contó una anécdota de su calle, lo avisó antes y volvió al punto principal; no se adelantó a sus propuestas ni perdió el hilo.

origin.audio: Last week I watched my cousin give a talk on the results of a neighbourhood survey. She opened with a joke, then outlined three parts: how the survey was carried out, what residents said about noise and traffic, and what she thinks the council should do. Halfway through, she digressed into a story about her own street, but she said so openly, apologised and returned to her main point. She finished with a short summary and invited questions.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula del orador con lo que hace en la charla.

pairs: I'd like to begin by outlining how the talk is organised.

pairs.es: anuncia el esquema de la charla

pairs: If I may digress for a moment, let me tell you about my street.

pairs.es: abre un paréntesis avisando al público

pairs: I'll touch on parking only briefly, since few people mentioned it.
To sum up, residents want quieter nights and safer crossings.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple un papel: anunciar el esquema, avisar de un desvío, tratar algo de pasada o cerrar con una síntesis.

pairs: I'd like to begin by outlining how the talk is organised.

pairs.es: anuncia el esquema de la charla

pairs: If I may digress for a moment, let me tell you about my street.

pairs.es: abre un paréntesis avisando al público

pairs: I'll touch on parking only briefly, since few people mentioned it.
To sum up, residents want quieter nights and safer crossings.

prompt.es: ¿Qué carencia señala sobre todo el comentario de la colega?

choices.text: Facts that were too few to justify the conclusions.
Too few signposts to show the plan and the ending.
A pace too rushed for the audience to follow the plan.

feedback.es: No sabía adónde iba la charla y el final la sorprendió: faltaban señales (signposts); los datos eran sólidos y nada se dice del ritmo.

origin.text: A colleague's feedback on a rehearsal: “Your facts were strong, but the talk felt like a list. I never knew where you were heading, and your last two minutes came as a complete surprise.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prioridad sugiere el plan de la oradora.

choices.text: Parking is the main concern, while noise gets a passing mention.
The method is the heart of the talk, and both issues are minor.
Noise is the main concern, while parking gets a passing mention.

feedback.es: Dedica una parte al ruido, la queja más repetida, y menciona el estacionamiento solo de pasada porque pocos vecinos lo plantearon: el ruido es la prioridad.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the speaker began by thanking everyone and promised to outline her findings in three parts. She would explain the method first, turn to noise next, the complaint that residents had mentioned most often, and touch on parking only briefly, since few people had raised it. She added that she might digress once or twice, but would always say so before returning to her main point. Last, she said, she would take questions.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué avisa de que quizá se desvíe.

choices.text: So listeners can follow her even when she leaves the plan.
So listeners can tell which points she considers unimportant.
So listeners are ready for her to run over the time allowed.

feedback.es: Avisar del desvío y volver al punto principal ayuda al público a seguir el hilo; no sirve para señalar lo poco importante ni para pedir más tiempo.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the speaker began by thanking everyone and promised to outline her findings in three parts. She would explain the method first, turn to noise next, the complaint that residents had mentioned most often, and touch on parking only briefly, since few people had raised it. She added that she might digress once or twice, but would always say so before returning to her main point. Last, she said, she would take questions.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mencionaría el costo solo de pasada y se centraría en el ruido.»

feedback.es: Touch on significa mencionar un tema sin detenerse en él; encaja con «only briefly» y con el informe que ya lo detalla.

origin.text: Her plan was clear from the start. She would ___ on the cost only briefly, because the report covers it in detail, and then spend most of the time on noise.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame hacer un paréntesis y luego volveré al punto.»

answer.text: Let me digress for a moment and then return to the point

feedback.es: Digress for a moment avisa del desvío y return to the point anuncia que el orador volverá al hilo principal.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la oradora ante quienes pedían más detalle sobre el costo?

choices.text: She concedes the point but hopes nobody asks about figures.
She concedes the point and promises to come back to it.
She insists the cost was already covered fully in the talk.

feedback.es: Reconoce la queja («I realise…»), se ofrece a volver sobre ello y admite que quizá no tenga todas las cifras: ni la esquiva ni la da por zanjada.

origin.text: So, to sum up: most residents want quieter nights, fewer cars and safer crossings. I realise some of you wanted more detail on the cost, and I'm happy to come back to that. Finally, I will take questions, although I may not have every figure to hand.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hará la oradora antes de explicar por qué importa el ruido.

choices.text: Explain in detail why noise matters to residents.
Go back to the method to justify the sample.
Comment briefly on the wording of the question.

feedback.es: «First, though» anuncia un paso previo: antes de explicar por qué importa el ruido, hará un comentario breve sobre cómo formularon la pregunta.

origin.audio: Right, that covers how we ran the survey, so let me move on to the results. Nearly two thirds of people mentioned noise, and I will come back to why that matters. First, though, a quick word about how we worded the question, because it changes what the numbers mean.

prompt.es: Completa: «En primer lugar, quiero explicar cómo recogimos los datos.»

feedback.es: Firstly abre la primera parte anunciada en el esquema, justo después de saludar y presentar la estructura.

origin.text: She had rehearsed carefully. After greeting the audience and outlining the structure, she said: “___, I want to explain how we collected the data.”

es: Describir cifras y tendencias de un gráfico con verbos de cambio, adverbios de intensidad y aproximaciones (rose sharply, a steady rise, fluctuate, plummet, account for, just under) y valorar lo que los datos permiten afirmar.

teaching.en: Bus use rose sharply in March, from roughly 2,000 to 3,500 passengers, before it began to level off at the end of spring.
teaching.es: El uso del autobús subió bruscamente en marzo, de unos 2.000 a 3.500 pasajeros, antes de empezar a estabilizarse a finales de primavera.
teaching.explanationEs: Rose sharply: verbo de subida + adverbio de intensidad; from… to… da el punto de partida y de llegada; level off = dejar de subir y estabilizarse.
segments: Bus use rose sharply in March, from roughly 2,000 to 3,500 passengers,
before it began to level off at the end of spring.
teaching.audioText: Bus use rose sharply in March, from roughly 2,000 to 3,500 passengers, before it began to level off at the end of spring.

teaching.en: The number of cyclists fell slightly between May and June, although the figure for the whole year was still higher than last year.
teaching.es: El número de ciclistas bajó ligeramente entre mayo y junio, aunque la cifra de todo el año seguía siendo mayor que la del año pasado.
teaching.explanationEs: Slightly describe un cambio pequeño; figure es la cifra o dato numérico; although introduce un contraste.
segments: The number of cyclists fell slightly between May and June, although the
figure for the whole year was still higher than last year.
teaching.audioText: The number of cyclists fell slightly between May and June, although the figure for the whole year was still higher than last year.

teaching.en: Train use grew gradually over the year, and there was a steady rise in tram passengers, from 900 to just over 1,200.
teaching.es: El uso del tren creció poco a poco durante el año, y hubo una subida constante de pasajeros de tranvía, de 900 a algo más de 1.200.
teaching.explanationEs: Gradually: cambio lento; a steady rise: sustantivo de tendencia + adjetivo; just over = algo más de.
segments: Train use grew gradually over the year, and there was a
steady rise in tram passengers, from 900 to just over 1,200.
teaching.audioText: Train use grew gradually over the year, and there was a steady rise in tram passengers, from 900 to just over 1,200.

teaching.en: Taxi use tends to fluctuate during the summer, and it can plummet when prices go up by almost twenty percent.
teaching.es: El uso del taxi tiende a fluctuar durante el verano y puede caer en picado cuando los precios suben casi un veinte por ciento.
teaching.explanationEs: Fluctuate: sube y baja sin rumbo claro; plummet: caída muy brusca; by + cifra indica cuánto cambia algo.
segments: Taxi use tends to fluctuate during the summer, and it
can plummet when prices go up by almost twenty percent.
teaching.audioText: Taxi use tends to fluctuate during the summer, and it can plummet when prices go up by almost twenty percent.

teaching.en: Commuters account for roughly forty percent of all passengers, while tourists account for only about ten percent.
teaching.es: Los viajeros habituales representan aproximadamente el cuarenta por ciento de los pasajeros, mientras que los turistas solo representan un diez por ciento.
teaching.explanationEs: Account for + porcentaje: la parte que un grupo representa del total; roughly y about aproximan.
segments: Commuters account for roughly forty percent of all passengers,
while tourists account for only about ten percent.
teaching.audioText: Commuters account for roughly forty percent of all passengers, while tourists account for only about ten percent.

teaching.en: The figure for taxis should remain steady at around 500 a day, unless the drop in tourist numbers continues.
teaching.es: La cifra de taxis debería mantenerse estable en torno a 500 al día, a menos que continúe la caída del número de turistas.
teaching.explanationEs: Remain steady: no cambia; drop es la caída como sustantivo y va seguida de in o of + lo que se mide.
segments: The figure for taxis should remain steady at around 500
a day, unless the drop in tourist numbers continues.
teaching.audioText: The figure for taxis should remain steady at around 500 a day, unless the drop in tourist numbers continues.

prompt.es: Elige la descripción más precisa de los datos de ciclismo.

choices.text: Cycling rose sharply in May, then remained steady in June.
Cycling rose gradually from April to June, by roughly ten percent.
Cycling rose sharply in May, then dropped slightly in June.

feedback.es: De abril a mayo la cifra se cuadruplica (cambio brusco) y de mayo a junio casi no cambia (410 frente a 400): se mantiene estable.

hint.es: Compara mayo con abril y luego junio con mayo: primero un cambio grande, después casi ninguno.

origin.text: A council report gives the monthly cycling figures: 100 riders in April, 400 in May and 410 in June.

prompt.es: Completa: «El uso del taxi tendía a fluctuar de una semana a otra.»

feedback.es: Fluctuate describe una cifra que sube y baja sin una dirección clara; por eso no se habla de tendencia.

hint.es: Verbo para algo que sube y baja sin rumbo fijo.

origin.text: Taxi use was irregular last summer. It tended to ___ from week to week, and then it fell sharply in October.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El uso del tranvía subió poco a poco de novecientos a unos mil doscientos.»

answer.text: Tram use rose gradually from nine hundred to roughly twelve hundred

feedback.es: Sujeto + verbo de cambio + adverbio + from… to…: roughly aproxima la cifra de llegada.

hint.es: Empieza con el sujeto Tram use y deja from… to… para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige a qué atribuye la oradora la subida del autobús.

choices.text: A sharp increase in the number of commuters.
A cut in fares introduced by the council.
The way train use grew gradually that year.

feedback.es: La oradora dice que el autobús subió bruscamente en marzo «after the council cut fares»: la causa es el recorte de tarifas, no el aumento de viajeros ni el tren.

origin.audio: In her presentation, the student explained that bus use had risen sharply in March, from two thousand to three and a half thousand passengers, after the council cut fares. Train use, by contrast, grew gradually over the whole year, while the figure for taxis remained steady at around five hundred a day. She pointed out that commuters account for roughly forty percent of all passengers, but she added that the data came from a single week, so she advised the audience to be careful with the trends.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada verbo o expresión con su significado al describir datos.

pairs: fluctuate

pairs.es: subir y bajar sin rumbo fijo

pairs: plummet
account for
remain steady

feedback.es: Cada expresión describe un comportamiento distinto de las cifras: irregular, caída brusca, proporción del total o estabilidad.

pairs: fluctuate

pairs.es: subir y bajar sin rumbo fijo

pairs: plummet
account for
remain steady

prompt.es: Completa: «Algo menos de la mitad de los encuestados usa el autobús.»

feedback.es: 98 de 200 es el 49 %: una aproximación por debajo de la mitad se dice just under (o nearly) half.

origin.text: The survey covered 200 people. Of these, 98 said they take the bus, so ___ half of the respondents are regular passengers.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe con más precisión los datos del museo.

choices.text: Numbers stayed steady over the summer, then fell slightly in September.
Numbers rose sharply over the summer, then plummeted in September.
Numbers stayed steady over the summer, then plummeted in September.

feedback.es: De junio a agosto la cifra casi no cambia (estable) y en septiembre baja de 1.010 a 600: una caída brusca, no ligera, después de un verano sin subida fuerte.

origin.text: Museum visitors: 1,000 in June, 1,000 in July, 1,010 in August and 600 in September, once the school holidays had ended.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le preocupa realmente a la autora del informe.

choices.text: That sales failed to recover in March as usual.
That sales fell by a third at the start of the year.
That sales fell further in March than in January.

feedback.es: La caída de enero es normal; lo que la inquieta es que la cifra de marzo apenas se mueva, señal de que no hay la recuperación habitual.

origin.audio: In her report, the author writes that sales plummeted by a third in January, but she adds that this is hardly surprising, since the same drop happens after every holiday season. What worries her more is the figure for March, which has hardly moved, because it suggests that the usual recovery has not happened this year.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los estudiantes representan aproximadamente un tercio de las respuestas.»

feedback.es: Account for + fracción o porcentaje expresa la parte que un grupo representa del total.

origin.text: The survey asked 400 people how they travel to work. Students ___ for roughly a third of the answers, while retired people made up only about one in ten.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La cifra del tranvía se mantuvo estable en torno a 900 todo el año.»

answer.text: The tram figure remained steady at around nine hundred all year

feedback.es: Remained steady describe una cifra que no cambia; at around + cifra da el nivel al que se mantuvo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere dar a entender el orador con este comentario sobre las ventas?

choices.text: That the rise shows the online strategy is working well.
That the rise matters less than it first seems.
That online sales will keep growing at the same pace.

feedback.es: Tras una caída brusca, una subida del 10 % solo recupera lo perdido: el orador relativiza el dato positivo.

origin.text: From the talk: “Online sales rose by about ten percent, which sounds good. However, the figure for the previous year had plummeted, so this year's rise mostly restores what was lost.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué describe mejor la evolución después de diciembre.

choices.text: A steady climb that continued through the whole winter.
A sharp jump followed by a slow fall back to normal.
Small ups and downs at a somewhat higher level.

feedback.es: Tras la ligera subida de diciembre la cifra oscila entre 450 y 500: sube y baja un poco, a un nivel algo superior al inicial.

origin.audio: The figure for museum visitors was steady at around four hundred a week, but it rose slightly in December and then fluctuated between four hundred and fifty and five hundred for the rest of the winter.

prompt.es: Completa las dos frases con el adverbio y el verbo adecuados.

feedback.es: Cuadruplicar una cifra exige un adverbio de cambio fuerte, y una cifra que no varía se describe con remained steady.

sentences: Sales rose ___ in March, from 100 to 400 units.
The price level ___ steady at around five percent all year.

title.en: Follow the structure of a talk
title.es: Seguir la estructura de una charla

es: Seguir la estructura de una charla en audio (apertura, puntos principales, desvíos y cierre), anotar sus puntos clave a partir de las señales del orador e inferir su postura.

teaching.en: The keynote speaker said she would cover three main points: cost, safety and comfort, and that she would spell out the key figures for each one.
teaching.es: La ponente principal dijo que abordaría tres puntos principales: el costo, la seguridad y la comodidad, y que explicaría con detalle las cifras clave de cada uno.
teaching.explanationEs: Cover + main points anuncia el esquema; spell out = explicar sin dar nada por sabido; anota cuántos puntos son.
segments: The keynote speaker said she would cover three main points: cost, safety and
comfort, and that she would spell out the key figures for each one.
teaching.audioText: The keynote speaker said she would cover three main points: cost, safety and comfort, and that she would spell out the key figures for each one.

teaching.en: After a short preamble about the school, the first key point was cost: a monthly ticket now costs forty euros, the main obstacle for students.
teaching.es: Tras un breve preámbulo sobre el colegio, el primer punto clave fue el costo: un pasaje mensual cuesta ahora cuarenta euros, el principal obstáculo para los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: The first key point is… abre el punto 1; el preámbulo no cuenta como punto; después viene el dato que conviene anotar.
segments: After a short preamble about the school, the first key point was cost:
a monthly ticket now costs forty euros, the main obstacle for students.
teaching.audioText: After a short preamble about the school, the first key point was cost: a monthly ticket now costs forty euros, the main obstacle for students.

teaching.en: Briefly, the second point was safety, and she went off on a tangent about street lighting, so some listeners began to lose track of the structure of the talk.
teaching.es: En pocas palabras, el segundo punto fue la seguridad, y se fue por la tangente con el alumbrado de las calles, así que algunos oyentes empezaron a perder el hilo de la estructura de la charla.
teaching.explanationEs: Briefly avisa de que el punto será corto; go off on a tangent = desviarse; lose track = perder el hilo.
segments: Briefly, the second point was safety, and she went off on a tangent about street
lighting, so some listeners began to lose track of the structure of the talk.
teaching.audioText: Briefly, the second point was safety, and she went off on a tangent about street lighting, so some listeners began to lose track of the structure of the talk.

teaching.en: To recap, she will wrap up by repeating the three points, so the audience can home in on one clear takeaway.
teaching.es: Para recapitular, cerrará repitiendo los tres puntos, de modo que el público pueda centrarse en una idea clara.
teaching.explanationEs: To recap señala el cierre; wrap up = concluir; home in on = centrarse en lo esencial, el mensaje que debe quedarte.
segments: To recap, she will wrap up by repeating the three points,
so the audience can home in on one clear takeaway.
teaching.audioText: To recap, she will wrap up by repeating the three points, so the audience can home in on one clear takeaway.

teaching.en: While I listen, I note down each key word, not full sentences, and when a speaker chooses to elaborate on a point, I add only one detail.
teaching.es: Mientras escucho, anoto cada palabra clave, no frases completas, y cuando un orador decide ampliar un punto, añado solo un detalle.
teaching.explanationEs: Note down + palabras clave; elaborate on = ampliar un punto con más detalle, que tú resumes en un solo dato.
segments: While I listen, I note down each key word, not full sentences, and when
a speaker chooses to elaborate on a point, I add only one detail.
teaching.audioText: While I listen, I note down each key word, not full sentences, and when a speaker chooses to elaborate on a point, I add only one detail.

teaching.en: A good listener notices when a speaker goes off on a tangent and waits for the signal that the main line has resumed.
teaching.es: Un buen oyente se da cuenta de cuándo el orador se va por la tangente y espera la señal de que se retoma la línea principal.
teaching.explanationEs: No todo lo que se dice es un punto del esquema: un desvío no se anota como punto principal.
segments: A good listener notices when a speaker goes off on a tangent
and waits for the signal that the main line has resumed.
teaching.audioText: A good listener notices when a speaker goes off on a tangent and waits for the signal that the main line has resumed.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué trata la charla y cómo se organiza.

choices.text: The library's opening hours, explained in detail.
The school library, divided into three points.
A comparison between the library and the canteen.

feedback.es: La oradora anuncia que abordará tres puntos principales sobre la biblioteca del colegio; el horario es solo uno de ellos y no compara con la cantina.

hint.es: Escucha la señal de apertura: dice el tema y cuántos puntos anuncia.

origin.audio: Hello, everyone. Today I will cover three main points about our school library: opening hours, books and study spaces, and I will spell out what each one would cost.

prompt.es: Completa: «El primer punto clave es el horario.»

feedback.es: The first key point is… abre el primer punto; key (o main) lo marca como una idea importante que conviene anotar.

origin.audio: Good morning, everyone. Today I will cover three main points about cycling to school: cost, safety and comfort. The first key point is cost. A bike becomes cheaper than a monthly bus pass after about ten months, and that matters to many families. Briefly, the second point is safety: since the new lane opened, accidents near the school have fallen by a third. Finally, comfort. I will spell out why students arrive calmer and more awake. To recap, cycling is cheaper, safer and healthier.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de tu charla con tres señalizadores y una tendencia.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club has grown. As you can see in my chart, membership rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of the members are first-year students, and just under a third are boys. Finally, I would like to turn to our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew gradually and is ready for a new challenge. The message I want you to take home is simple: a few friends and a corridor were enough. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.
accepted: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club has grown. As you can see in my chart, membership rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of the members are first-year students, and just under a third are boys. Finally, I would like to turn to our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew gradually and is ready for a new challenge. The message I want you to take home is simple: a few friends and a corridor were enough. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.

Hello, everyone, and welcome. Today I want to present my hobby, which is running, and I will outline the talk in three parts: why I started, how my training changed and my next goal. Firstly, I started running two years ago because I wanted to feel healthier. At the beginning, I could run for only ten minutes without stopping. Let's move on to the second part: my training. As you can see in my chart, my weekly distance rose gradually, from roughly five to around twenty kilometres in one year. I also take a short pause between exercises, and I keep a steady pace. Now I'd like to turn to my goal for next year. I hope to run a half marathon in the spring, and my friends will run with me. To sum up, running is cheap, simple and good for the head as well as for the body. Thank you very much for listening. Are there any questions?

feedback.es: Un buen guion abre con saludo y tema, usa tres señalizadores, describe una tendencia con cifras y cierra con To sum up y una invitación a preguntas.

origin.text: When several listeners began to ___ back against her conclusion, she thanked them and answered each objection calmly.

prompt.es: Escribe tu presentación final con dos respuestas matizadas.

answer.text: To sum up my talk, I presented a study of 120 students who slept eight hours a night for a month. Their marks rose steadily, from 7.1 to 7.8, and the effect was clear for most of them. Now let me answer your two questions. First, you asked how many of the students were girls. Off the top of my head, it was around half, but I'm afraid I don't have the exact figure, so I would need to check the report before I give you an accurate number. Second, you asked whether these students were simply better students already. That is a fair challenge. To a certain extent you may be right, because the students chose to take part. However, the marks of the same students rose during the study, so the findings suggest that sleep may help, although I would add one caveat: the sample was small, and more research is needed before we can be sure. I can give you more detail after the talk, and I will send the full figures by email. Thank you for your questions.

Let me summarise the main points of my talk. We studied 120 students for a month. Those who slept eight hours scored higher, and their mark went up from 7.1 to 7.8. Thank you for your two questions. About the first one, how many girls took part, I'm afraid I can't give an accurate number now, but I can check it and send you the figure later. About the second one, it could be argued that these students were already better, and that is a fair point. However, the same students improved during the month, so the results seem to show a real effect. It is likely to be valid for students of our age, although I would not say it is certain, and I would add one caveat: the sample was small. I can give you more detail after the talk, and I will send the full numbers by email this week.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta resume la charla con tendencia y cifras, admite con honestidad que no tienes un dato exacto, y reconoce la objeción sin perder la conclusión.

origin.text: Caso: acabas de presentar un estudio sobre 120 estudiantes que durmieron ocho horas durante un mes; su nota media subió de 7,1 a 7,8. El público te hace dos preguntas: 1) «¿Cuántas chicas participaron?» (no recuerdas la cifra exacta) y 2) «¿No serían ya mejores estudiantes?». Escribe entre 210 y 260 palabras: un resumen con la tendencia y las cifras, y dos respuestas con matiz (una salvedad incluida).

feedback.es: Reconoce que la muestra era pequeña y por eso presentó el patrón como provisional («tentative»): acepta la limitación y mantiene una afirmación prudente, sin retirarla ni exagerarla.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el orador ante la pregunta.

choices.text: He admits what his data cannot show and adds cautious context.
He admits his data are limited and says the question is unimportant.
